reviewer: Claude review agent, independent of the extraction agent; no human review claimed. Separate Claude (Opus 5) agent on branch claude/uc-hitdisc; the extraction agent that built this batch did not take part.
scope: Independent review of use-case-coverage-hitdisc-20261022 (extraction commit 161dc5b) for rewire-benchmark-data #177: 1,375 records as reviewed (1,091 results, 127 evaluations, 81 configurations, 29 claims, 12 protocols, 10 datasets, 9 sources, 6 benchmarks, 5 dataset subsets, 4 methods, 1 use case), of which the extraction pass left 1,366 and this review added 9 metadata-correction claims. All nine source artifacts were re-downloaded and their SHA-256 matched. The extractor's extract/build_batch.py was not run: three parsers written for this review (review/myparse_shen.py, review/myparse_xlsx.py, review/compare.py) re-parsed Shen et al. Tables 1 to 5 from the pinned JATS XML and CACHE #3 sheet S8 from xl/worksheets/sheet9.xml, and compared all 1,091 printed values, their locators' row labels and column headers, and all 332 raw_xml_value strings, with 0 mismatches. review/coverage_check.py proved the batch covers exactly the 1,082 printed table cells, none duplicated, omitted or invented, plus the 9 body-text values. 48 values were then checked by hand against the raw markup. The 12 relevance judgements, the draft summary, the seven descriptive claims, the use-case record and the six metric concepts added to data/vocab/metric.ttl were checked against their sources.

by_source.kim2026 Results body text: 9 printed AUC strings, all present verbatim; the XML holds no table-wrap element
by_source.cache3-si002 sheet S8 own selection: 161 cells (columns D to J, 23 workflows), all match including raw_xml_value
by_source.cache3-si002 sheet S8 merged library: 171 cells (columns L to T, 19 workflows), all match including raw_xml_value

manual_sample.method: Each sampled value was read from the raw markup (the <tr> elements of the JATS tables, the <row> elements of xl/worksheets/sheet9.xml, the Results paragraphs of the Kim et al. XML) rather than through either parser.

corrections: hitdisc-20261022-source-litpcba-audit: evidence_concerns removed. The LIT-PCBA leakage audit is the source reporting the problem, not a source with a problem, and because the use case and its summary cite it the entry withheld all twelve judgements and the summary (shared/omics/use-cases.ts cleanSource). Its finding is kept as the leakage-audit claim, as limitations on the LIT-PCBA benchmark and the five-target protocol, and as a source warning on each of the 84 LIT-PCBA results.
hitdisc-20261022-source-litpcba-page: the totals-conflict evidence_concerns entry now names both artifact hashes, not only the page's.

84 Shen Table 4 results: source_warnings added for the LIT-PCBA leakage audit and for the unresolved actives-to-inactives conflict between the official page (7761/382674) and Shen et al. (10030/2798737), with both hashes and locators. EF and NEF both depend on that ratio.

57 CACHE #3 normalised merged-library results (sheet S8 columns R, S and T): metric_qualifier corrected to the stored formula and source_warnings rewritten. The cells are stored as 1000*N/L, 1000*O/L and R+S, so each is confirmed Tier 1 or Tier 2 hits per 1000 compounds predicted active. The previous qualifier said only 'normalised value' and hid the per-1000 scaling.

data/vocab/metric.ttl, :cache-challenge-normalized-hit-score: definition and scope note corrected to the stored formula. The previous definition quoted the Figure 6c caption ('the aggregated score of all compounds predicted active divided by the number of compounds predicted to be actives'), which the formulas contradict: the numerator is a count of confirmed tier hits, not an aggregated score, and the caption omits the factor of 1000.
hitdisc-20261022-protocol-cache3-merged-library: metric_definition and two limitations corrected; the article's internal inconsistency about Figure 6b added as a limitation.

hitdisc-20261022-protocol-cache3-own-selection: the 'source prints no per-workflow hit rate' limitation corrected (none for this arm, but columns R, S and T are rates for the merged-library arm), and the zero-score limitation added.

54 CACHE #3 own-selection score results: source_warnings added. For the twelve workflows with no confirmed hit the workbook stores 0 for score of best hit, aggregated score and top novelty score; a 0 there means there was no hit to score, not a hit scored at zero.

hitdisc-20261022-use-case-summary and hitdisc-20261022-use-case-mapping-cache3-merged-library: the WF1696 wording corrected to the source's own. 'Significantly more hits than any other' is what the article says of WF1715's own-selection aggregated score; of WF1696 it says it 'did better than any other method in retrieving hits from the collection of all molecules selected in Round 1'.
use-case-hit-discovery-virtual-screening: evidence_checked.records now names this pass's dated review, as docs/use-cases.md requires.

The five LIT-PCBA dataset_subset records: used_in retargeted from the five-target dataset to hitdisc-20261022-protocol-shen-litpcba5. shared/omics/relations.ts defines used_in as data to an assessment, so a dataset is not a legal target and the store refused the batch; each subset's parent dataset was already in attributes.source_dataset. The extraction pass's shape checker reported that every link resolves to a record of an allowed kind, but did not check the relation's from-kind and to-kind pair.
Nine metadata-correction-* claims keep the previous value of every descriptive field and link changed above.
upheld_without_change: All nine source artifact hashes matched on re-download; no mismatch to raise.

All 1,091 printed values, numeric values, locators, metric concepts, qualifiers, directions, unit concepts and the configuration and protocol each result hangs off are correct as extracted. No value was changed and no superseding result was needed.

Every null is genuinely unstated in the pinned source, and no missing value is recorded as zero: the four CACHE workflows with blank merged-library cells carry no result at all, and the blank carboxylic-acid-penalty column and the unheaded rank column are recorded as claims rather than as results.

The extraction pass's correction that CACHE #3's relevant figure is Figure 6 and not Figure 5, that panel c carries the 'divided by the number of compounds predicted to be actives' wording, and that columns D and E must not be divided, is upheld. Its further claim that CACHE #3 publishes no per-workflow hit rate is overturned: see corrections.

The extraction pass's correction that DUD-E uses 50 property-matched decoys per clustered ligand is upheld from the abstract, and the search pass's estimate of about 1:60 appears nowhere in the batch, the batch documents or the vocabulary.

enrichment-factor, normalized-enrichment-factor, bedroc, cache-challenge-activity-score and cache-challenge-novelty-score are faithful to the sources that print them; the NEF definition is quoted verbatim from Shen Table 4 footnote a and reference 71 is Truchon and Bayly 2007, so the BEDROC attribution is verifiable from the pinned artifact. Declining to invent a STATO closeMatch is right.

All twelve relevance judgements are upheld: the five prospective wet-lab arms as direct and the seven retrospective or cost arms as proxy. Every protocol records its actives-to-decoys ratio and decoy construction, and every judgement says raw enrichment factors are not comparable across benchmarks.

The seven reviewer_must_judge design decisions are upheld: keeping the Table 2 reprints with their source warnings, one evaluation per configuration and protocol with per-target cells distinguished by qualifier, CACHE workflows as parentless configurations, three CACHE metric concepts at the current granularity, printed_value as the shortest round-tripping decimal with raw_xml_value alongside, the CACHE own-selection arm as direct with its self-selection confound first, and a judgement for the GPCRrecent six-target protocol.

The draft summary is descriptive, makes no recommendation, names the decoy construction of each benchmark and carries the leakage audit on every LIT-PCBA figure. Every figure in it was matched to a result record and to the pinned source; one sentence of attribution was wrong and is corrected.
The use_case record carries every field docs/use-cases.md requires.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent. It is not human scientific review, not qualified domain review, and not reproduction of any result.
Transcription was checked against the pinned bytes. Nothing was recomputed from primary data, no model was run and no experiment was repeated.

evidence_concerns is declared for source records only in shared/omics/attribute-registry.ts, and source_warnings for result records only, so the LIT-PCBA leakage audit could not be recorded as an evidence_concerns entry on the benchmark or dataset records as the review brief asked. It is recorded as the leakage-audit claim, as limitations on the benchmark and the protocol, and as a source warning on each of the 84 LIT-PCBA results.

No figure was read: Shen et al. Figures 1 to 5 and S1 to S17 (including the ligand-similarity leakage analysis), Table 6 and tables S1 and S2; Kim et al. Figures 3 and 5 and their supplements; CACHE #3 Figures 2 to 9, sheets S1 to S7 of ci5c02441_si_002.xlsx, the whole of ci5c02441_si_003.xlsx and the Supporting Information PDF.
The LIT-PCBA leakage audit was read as an abstract only; its own tables were not retrieved, so no per-target memorisation-baseline value is recorded.

Five closed-access primaries were not retrieved by either pass: DEKOIS 2.0 and 1.0, the LIT-PCBA primary paper, TocoDecoy, and the CACHE #1 and #2 results papers. Eight of Shen Table 1's 24 arms are quoted from references 34, 35, 36, 38 and 39, none of which was resolved, so no evaluation of those tools is independent of that compilation.
The LIT-PCBA actives-to-inactives conflict is left unresolved and marked. It withholds the shen-litpcba5 judgement, by design.

The CACHE #3 article contradicts itself about Figure 6b, calling it a hit rate in the Results text and an aggregated score in the caption. Recorded, not resolved; no value in this batch comes from Figure 6.
The store now carries the auroc concept on a 0-to-1 scale from Shen et al. and a 0-to-100 scale from Kim et al.; unit_detail distinguishes them.

No baseline claim was added. Docking alone would satisfy the definition in docs/use-cases.md, and a claim naming Glide SP, Gnina, GOLD CHEMPLP, LeDock, Surflex-Dock and DOCK3.7 is recommended for a later pass, but a review should not author a judgement it would then review.

derivation_check.method: Ran deriveUseCaseInputs over the loaded store after the batch was added, rather than reading the blocker conditions off the code.
derivation_check.withheld_reason: a cited source is unchecked or has evidence concerns, and no evaluation on the protocol is eligible: the judgement cites hitdisc-20261022-source-litpcba-page and so does the five-target dataset, so each of its evaluations is ineligible under evaluationBlocker. The unresolved actives-to-inactives conflict is the cause and the withholding is intended.
derivation_check.before_the_audit_concern_was_removed: all twelve judgements and the summary would have been withheld, because the use case and the summary cite the audit source.
